sources_tested: Canon 0825.001; targeted Snell/TrGF bibliographic checks; exact local Perseus Greek Anthology TEI `tlg7000.tlg001.perseus-grc9`, AG 11.246; CTS metadata and canonical-greekLit CC BY-SA 4.0 licence; independent scholarly/title confirmations.
open_text_result: Exact open ancient testimony available: Lucillius, AG 11.246.6, names Meliton and his Niobe (‘γράψει μʼ ὡς Νιόβην δρᾶμα σαπρὸν Μελίτων’). It securely supplies the otherwise lost play’s title, but preserves no verse from Meliton’s drama.
scan_result: No scan retained: the title testimony is already available in a licensed TEI; the 1971 TrGF edition is modern and was not treated as a reusable scan source.
next_action: Retain the complete six-line Lucillius witness only as title testimony, with Perseus/Paton attribution and CC BY-SA 4.0 notice; catalogue `Niobe` as the title and do not represent it as surviving text of Meliton.
notes: The Canon’s generic ‘Titulus’ is resolvable: the cited AG line calls the anticipated play a Niobe. The TEI identifies the epigrammatist as Lucillius, so the source is not an author-text match for TLG 0825; it is an exact external witness to the title. Modern scholarship notes that the poet is otherwise unknown and that no plot or dramatic verse survives.
